title: Unveiling the Human Virome post Kidney Transplantation – Insights into Shifting Viral Landscapes and Potential Health Consequences
summary: Lifelong immunosuppressive maintenance therapy is mandatory following kidney transplantation to prevent graft rejection and minimize risks for graft failure. However, immunosuppression is associated with side effects and complications, such as the occurrence of recurring, sometimes fatal infections, or an increased risk of tumor diseases. After the initiation of immunosuppressive therapy, changes in the balance of human viruses, called the human virome, occur. Until now, limited research has been conducted on the human virome and its changes post kidney transplantation, but understanding its role in disease pathogenesis may offer new diagnostic and therapeutic opportunities.
